item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04. Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month . But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop." The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser. The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years." Another important benefit is "atomic, transactional updates," which he said "brings enormous stability." The terminology comes from the database world : an atomic operation succeeds as a whole or is not applied. The aim is to avoid leaving the system stranded between incompatible package versions, with rollback providing a route back if an update causes trouble. The "composable" part means assembling the OS from separately packaged components, from desktop environments to underlying services such as PipeWire and fingerprint-reader support. Here, Seager used an example that spoke to us. He asked: "Ever installed something and watch as it spewed stuff all over your system?" Yes, we have, many, many times. You install one innocent-seeming little component, and it brings in a database, three new server components, and about half of a different desktop environment. We mentioned an example when we described how to customize Xfce a couple of months ago. That time around, in Debian, we found it was safe to install all packages starting with "xfce4-" except "xfce4-dev-tools." Most are tiny panel controls taking just hundreds of kilobytes, but the "dev-tools" package also pulls in several hundred megabytes of compilers, linkers, and other programming tools, totally unrelated to desktop layouts – and once installed, they're surprisingly tricky to remove again. This is part of the appeal of a composable immutable OS: adding a component need not mean tangling its dependencies into the base system. But easier housekeeping isn't the only attraction. Canonical kept snap packages from its cancelled phone and tablet OS because snaps enable it to maintain a single package of, for instance, Firefox, which will work on all of its different OS versions that are still getting updates. Moving such important external dependencies into isolated snap packages makes it easier and safer to upgrade from one version of the OS to another. Complex sets of dependencies are the main point of failure of OS upgrades, especially when the OS has been used for a while. This is very much not a solved problem. For instance, Debian version upgrades can be fraught – especially when the installation has decades of history behind it . Debian does at least support version-to-version upgrades. For many years and versions, RHEL did not – which is why we highlighted AlmaLinux's tooling for the task . Zorin OS added version-to-version upgrades in 16.3 just a few years ago. Linux Mint introduced its own upgrade tooling a few years earlier, although it still imposes restrictions . It's a tough issue to crack. Major enterprise vendors discourage it, and phone OSes are all immutable. Helping with this problem is one of the main reasons snap packaging exists, while Flatpak is almost entirely irrelevant to it. Seager also stated that Core Desktop would support "multiple desktops from the start." This will not be a GNOME-only project. Indeed, he specifically mentioned a KDE Plasma version, saying: "Plasma is great. People love it. We will have a KDE edition, with rolling Plasma. We will deliver upstream Plasma, as fast as we can." That sounds like a very welcome counterpoint to the LTS version of Plasma 6.6 in Kubuntu 26.04 whose announcement we covered back in August. For the "attestable" line of the slide, he claimed that Core Desktop was "evolving the way we think about 'trust' on a machine. We have TPM, secure boot, TPM-backed Full Disk Encryption… but they're all bolt-ons." Core Desktop, he added, could "tie this into a hardware root of trust," delivering "verified system integrity." Canonical revived its TPM-backed full-disk encryption system back in 2025 , and it arrived in Ubuntu 26.04. Back in January, systemd creator Lennart Poettering launched his startup Amutable, and earlier this month published a technical overview of its new immutable Linux . We suspect Canonical is watching closely, and that this is a hint in that direction. We were also amused by Seager's mention of another rather niche distro: he said that Core Desktop would deliver "all of the joy that people derive from NixOS, for those with that perverse habit – but for everybody." Daily preview installation images of Core Desktop will, apparently, be available very soon, in both GNOME and KDE flavors, and he warned that "there be dragons." (That may be a veiled nod to one of founder Mark Shuttleworth's other companies .) After the promises made in 2023 , we'll be watching that timetable closely. "I believe this is the future of Linux," Seager said, promising "a final version by 28.04, released alongside Ubuntu," adding that a "very stretchy stretch goal was by default for 30.04: download from ubuntu.com and you get Core Desktop – unless you ask for the other thing." For those alarmed by that prospect, he had reassurance: "Ubuntu as you know it today is not going anywhere. There are no plans for the existing distro to go away." item.title: ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed
item.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. item.content:encoded: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. He argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence. Similarly, African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu said Nigerians were rejecting Tinubu because they were experiencing the effects of his administration’s economic policies. Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, made the remarks on Thursday during an appearance on *Politics Today*. He linked the growing public discontent to the hardship Nigerians had experienced since the removal of the petrol subsidy. Tinubu, who assumed office in May 2023, is seeking re-election in 2027. He is expected to face opposition from Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The post ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 72 Years Later, Lord of the Rings Officially Reveals Why Sauron Is So Evil
item.description: Sauron is one of the most famous villains of all time, but The Lord of the Rings doesn’t really explore why the Dark Lord is so obsessed with conquering all of Middle-earth. The prequel series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has been working to make Sauron (Charlie Vickers) more complex — which isn’t hard since he gets to have conversations with other characters rather than solely appear as an ominous eye. He’s a master of deception who has appeared in multiple guises to further his schemes, but in one of the latest episodes released Wednesday, Sauron gets honest and reveals his true motivations.

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Continue reading...

item.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
item.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs. And its enormous iron core , much bigger proportionally than the core of any other planet in the solar system, makes its very formation and evolution a puzzle. If all goes well, BepiColombo will start to unravel the convoluted tale of our solar system’s smallest planet .

item.title: Support tech fixed malware by charging client less for their services
item.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. It’s still on his desk!" Have you done less tech support to deliver more value? If so, click here to send On Call an email and charge us with the responsibility of telling your story on a future Friday. ®

item.title: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo officially enter FIFA presidential race
item.description: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

item.title: Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation
item.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa The Nigeria Customs Service, NCS and Federal Customs Service of Russia have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement, while exploring mutual recognition of their Authorised Economic Operator, AEO programmes. The service in a statement said the Agreement on Cooperation and Mutual Assistance in Customs Matters, CMAA provides a framework for collaboration in customs procedures, information exchange, financial integrity, border security and personnel capacity development. Speaking, Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, who led the Nigerian delegation, described the agreement as a strategic instrument for safeguarding economic integrity, securing supply chains and strengthening trade governance. He explained that the signing followed months of technical consultations, legal reviews and constructive engagements between both administrations. Adeniyi explained that the NCS had accelerated its digital transformation through the adoption of electronic systems for customs declarations, payments and submission of supporting documents. According to him, the reforms demonstrate that revenue generation and trade facilitation can complement each other, in line with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards. On the implementation of the agreement, the Customs boss identified cooperation between the two countries’ AEO programmes as a major priority. He said both administrations would exchange experiences on their respective frameworks and operational procedures, with the long-term objective of achieving mutual recognition to facilitate the movement of cargo and reward compliant traders. The two sides also explored arrangements for exchanging customs statistics and trade data to improve analysis of bilateral trade flows. Adeniyi disclosed that Nigeria was participating in the World Customs Organisation’s data initiative. Russia’s Head of Customs, Valery Pikalyov, explained that his administration was authorised to collect and exchange customs statistics derived from declarations. Pikalyov expressed readiness to explore a dedicated data-sharing arrangement with Nigeria. The agreement also provides for cooperation against customs offences, illicit financial flows, grey-market importations, tax evasion, counterfeit goods, narcotics and other prohibited or hazardous materials. It further establishes a framework for direct operational assistance, personnel training and the exchange of professional expertise between the two administrations. The post Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
item.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. item.title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process. Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday. He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980. The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole. “Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. “They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo. “I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives. “There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. “I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process. “Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.” The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved. “I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. “The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government. “For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology. “People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government? “These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night. “But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. “In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. Forty-six years later, we are gathered in one of the institutions that grew from that decision. And generations of young people have gained opportunities that might otherwise have been beyond their reach,” he stated. Mbah noted that beyond the establishment of ESUT, the Nwobodo Administration encouraged communities to build schools, with government providing teachers and other support. “He also invested in industry, seeking to create employment and strengthen the state’s productive capacity. “Some of those industries later fell into decline, and today we are working to bring a number of them back into use. “The value of such decisions is ultimately found in people’s lives. A child who could attend school in their own community. A young person who became the first in their family to enter university. A household supported by employment in a local industry,” he stated. He hailed generations of academics, administrators and staff, who have sustained ESUT through changing governments, difficult economic circumstances and the demands of educating successive generations. “In this regard, I want to assure the university community that the Enugu State Government is committed to the full implementation of the Academic Staff Union of Universities’ agreement with the Federal Government. “We are already speaking with legislators to firm up its inclusion in the budget for implementation as soon as possible,” he assured. Meanwhile, a major highpoint of the event was the conferment of an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Leadership, Governance, and Human Capital Development on Nwobodo. ESUT’s Vice Chancellor, Prof. Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, said it was in appreciation of the ex-governor’s huge contributions to the development of Enugu State, but also the entire old Anambra State, listing his many achievements. Another highpoint was the unveiling of Senator Nwobodo’s iconic status and the commissioning of a newly constructed road, Dr. Peter Mbah Drive, by the Governor. item.title: Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State. Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm. The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post. According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops. He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away. Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him. He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital. Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested. He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace. Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction. “We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said. He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected. “Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. The post Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026. President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.” Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries. “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said. The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities. He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns. Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026. “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024. “By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said. He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites. Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025. He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics. The post FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments
item.description: By Henry Ojelu President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments. He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN. President Tinubu at the launch of a six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, organised to celebrate the senior lawyer’s 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as an SAN, said: “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies its judges only weakens its own foundation. “This administration passed the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024, reversing over 15 years of stagnation and delivering a 300 percent increase in the salaries of our Judicial Officers of the Superior Court of record. “We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading. “We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured. Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence. “Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said. He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship. Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession. The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades. “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said. Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged. He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented. “Presidents change. Parties change. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading. “We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured. Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence. “Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said. He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship. Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession. The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades. “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said. Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged. He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented. “Presidents change. Parties change. The Lead Counsel remains,” he said. President of the Senate Godswill Akpabio lauded President Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy, and national development. He assured the President that the National Assembly will continue to support all legal instruments that will promote justice, democracy and the rule of law. He also commended Chief Olanipekun for his contributions to the legal profession. Similarly, the Chief Justice of the Federation, Justice Kudirat Kere-Ekun, praised Wole Olanipekun for his immense contributions to the legal profession, believing that the publications being unveiled will further contribute to the intellectual depth, advocacy and enrichment of the nation’s jurisprudence. The Attorney-General of the Federation and Justice Minister, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, also spoke glowingly of Olanipekun and recalled several times they collaborated in court. As a lawyer, you don’t want to be on the opposite side of Chief Olanipekun, he said. Governor Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State eulogised Wole Olanipekun for enriching the legal profession, saying Ekiti State was proud of him. Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, also gave a goodwill message. Chief Wole Olanipekun recalled his personal relationship with President Tinubu over the years and commended the President for his steadfastness, advocacy for democracy, and sacrifices. He revealed that at one such meeting, the President taught him the difference between legal and political jurisprudence. In his keynote address titled “The Rule of Law As a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth”, Tony Elumelu said the rule of law was vital to private sector growth and attraction of foreign investment, as entrepreneurs and investors were concerned about the right application of law as well as fair and speedy arbitration. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said: “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives were often overlooked, adding that the country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished,” “Nigeria is a scam,” and “Nigeria happened to me,” warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost was beyond reputational damage as, according to him, investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, postponement of expansion plans by businesses and seeking of opportunities elsewhere by talented Nigerians. He, however, acknowledged that citizens had the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism, stressing that the country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress. “Government and businesses cannot rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. PR can’t cover bad leadership, global experts warn Meanwhile, global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures. Trust, they said, could not be bought with publicity but earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises. The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, organised in Abuja by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations. The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America, and moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub. For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership was shown in personal conduct, not public declarations. To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right, even when nobody was watching. From Asia-Pacific, the chair, Jaffri Osman, said effective leadership required more than intellectual intelligence, adding that motional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities. “Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said. Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly. item.title: Dangote cement records 60% reduction in road traffic accidents
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations. The milestone was announced at the 2026 Customer Truck Scheme, CTS, Annual Driver Safety Award and Recognition Programme, where the company celebrated drivers who demonstrated exemplary safety performance and maintained accident-free records throughout the assessment period. The achievement builds on an earlier 30 percent reduction in road traffic accidents recorded in 2023, following the introduction of the company’s Safety Improvement Plan. As part of the initiative, approximately 3,000 drivers were trained in defensive driving techniques and safe road-use practices. According to the company, the sustained decline in accidents reflects the effectiveness of continuous driver training, behavioural monitoring, corrective interventions, and the deliberate recognition of safe driving practices. Speaking at the event on behalf of the Group Sales and Marketing Director, the National Sales Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Mr. Dolapo Ali, noted that the rapid expansion of the company’s transportation operations had made road safety a critical business priority. He disclosed that the CTS fleet had grown significantly from 469 trucks in 2017 to over 2,500 trucks today, increasing the need for a more structured and proactive safety management approach. “Our business has experienced tremendous growth over the years, and with that growth comes greater responsibility. As the number of trucks and drivers operating across our roads increases, so too does our exposure to road safety risks. Protecting lives and ensuring safe operations must therefore remain at the heart of our transport strategy,” he stated. Ali explained that road traffic accidents peaked in 2021 and 2022, prompting the company to introduce its Safety Improvement Plan in early 2023. A key component of the programme was an intensive defensive-driving training initiative through which approximately 3,000 drivers received professional safety training. The intervention delivered immediate results, with accident rates declining by 30 per cent in 2023 compared to the previous year, followed by a further 60 per cent reduction thereafter. To strengthen compliance and encourage safer driving behaviour, Dangote Cement also deployed advanced telematics technology across its fleet operations. The system enables real-time monitoring of critical driving behaviours, including overspeeding, harsh braking, and aggressive acceleration. item.title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe & Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency. Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday. Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday. Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October. The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026. Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves. He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market. “With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said. Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows. Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply. “The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said. Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency. He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows. item.title: ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa
item.description: THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals. Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-generation banks, has expressed sadness over Ajasa’s demise, saying his death is a loss not only to Vanguard but also to the media industry. In a condolence letter by its Group Head, Brand and Corporate Communication, Dafe Ivwurie, the bank said: “We were deeply saddened to learn of the death of Olufemi Ajasa. “By all accounts, he was an accomplished and highly respected digital journalist whose professionalism, dedication, and commitment to excellence contributed immensely to the growth and reputation of Vanguard’s digital media platforms. His passing at such a young age is a great loss not only to Vanguard but also to the Nigerian media industry.” Meanwhile, Obe, who took to his Facebook page to mourn Ajasa, described him as one of the first journalists trained at his clinic. He recounted the events that brought him close to the deceased and traced the history of their relationship until Ajasa’s death on Sunday. Obe said: “Circa 1997, TaijoWonukabe Limited, which I co-founded about two years earlier, moved from its garage office graciously donated to us by the prolific columnist, late Pini Jason Onyegbadue, into a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, in Surulere, Lagos. “That property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Sam Amuka-Pemu, the legendary journalist, Uncle Sam. “One day, not long after we moved in, Uncle Sam showed up, to greet Madam Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow on the same premises. “I knew him then more by name than physical interactions. Either when he was leaving or as he alighted, I approached him, to introduce myself and after we exchanged pleasantries, he said: Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building. “From that day till date, we became connected. Fast forward to circa 2015: I had founded The Journalism Clinic and converted and renamed the hall which was the finishing room of PrintPro Projects Limited – the printing subsidiary of TaijoWonukabe – to The Hub – the training room of The Journalism Clinic at Anifowose, around the corner from Bassie Ogamba. “Uncle Sam visited one afternoon and declared ‘Vanguard will send people to all the training you will do here’.” He kept his word and the first paid training we had in The Hub included three participants from Vanguard Online Desk and Olufemi Ajasa was one of them. “A fine gentleman, two days ago, Vanguard reported his passing after a brief illness. Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed. This really hit hard. item.title: Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP
item.description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria. This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country. Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings. He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs. Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers. Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries. The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors. These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses. President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments. The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 20 – V-G-R
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity’s most distant interstellar spacecraft ? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day . In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. For extra credit, fans of math can calculate that at one light-day per 50 years, Voyager 1 will reach its one light-year (365 light-days) distance milestone in about 18,250 years. item.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Stormy Southwest Pacific Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa. item.content:encoded: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Stormy Southwest Pacific Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa. Xavier is likely one of the first of several storms to affect the region in the coming months. A seasonal outlook from the Fiji Meteorological Service projects that the region could see between 11 and 15 named tropical cyclones this season, with the greatest risk east of the international date line. Storm activity in the Southwest Pacific basin typically peaks in February . NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview . item.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
item.description: From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.” It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in two versions: a “dark” mix by US producer Tchad Blake and a “bright” version that’s the handiwork of Mike “Spike” Stent, famed for working with everyone from U2 and Madonna to Frank Ocean and Harry Styles. item.title: From Dancehall to Rumba, Rema Stretches His Sound on New EP “E-Mortal Boy (EMB)” | Listen
item.description: Rema releases his seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy (EMB), featuring Wizkid, Theodora, BNYX, and Kah-Lo. Photo Credit: Rema/Instagram For weeks, Rema has been teasing us with a new project—first came “ TEA ” and then “ Oh No “, and if you have had those on repeat on your playlist, you now have the entire package with his seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ). Ever since his self-titled debut EP in 2019, the Benin-born star has never been interested in staying boxed into one sound. Following his 2023 EP Ravage and his 2024 Grammy-nominated album HEIS , he uses this new seven-song collection to pull rhythms from across the Black diaspora into one bold, genre-hopping ride. If you already had “TEA” on loop when its dancehall bounce, glossy pop, and techno twists took over the Nigerian timeline, or kept “Oh No” close for that percussion-heavy Rvssian groove about a lover’s mixed signals, they both sit right inside the full lineup alongside five more records . The biggest headline moment opens the project: “ Feel Alright ” pairs Rema with Wizkid for their very first official joint release, a smooth ballad about satisfying a lover’s appetite. From there, he switches gears across “ Velvet “, where rumba drums meet slick guitar riffs as he vows to take on the world for someone special, and “ TANZANIA “, a BNYX-assisted track with Bollywood score-inspired flair. The rest of the EP keeps that same adventurous streak alive. On “ SUGA “, Rema teams up with French Congolese singer Theodora for a rougher, grunge-leaning sound, before closing out on “ Bang Bang ” with longtime collaborator London and Nigerian dance music favourite Kah-Lo . Nearly a decade into his run, Rema still sounds completely locked in on what comes next, leaving you with seven quick tracks to drop straight into your weekend rotation. Listen below ﻿ The post From Dancehall to Rumba, Rema Stretches His Sound on New EP “E-Mortal Boy (EMB)” | Listen appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .
